bottom_line: Apixaban (5 mg twice daily) versus warfarin (INR 2.0 to 3.0) reduced stroke or systemic embolism (hazard ratio with apixaban, 0.79; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.66 to 0.95).
implications: Based on the reported hazard ratios and event rates, the trial supports that in this studied atrial fibrillation population, apixaban reduced stroke or systemic embolism versus warfarin (1.27%/yr vs 1.60%/yr; HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.66 to 0.95) and reduced major bleeding (2.13%/yr vs 3.09%/yr; HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.60 to 0.80) and death from any cause (3.52%/yr vs 3.94%/yr; HR 0.89, 95% CI 0.80 to 0.99). The reported ischemic or uncertain type of stroke comparison did not show a statistically significant difference (HR 0.92; 95% CI, 0.74 to 1.13; P = 0.42), so these data do not by themselves establish a reduction for that specific stroke subtype.

major_points.quote: In this randomized, double-blind trial, we compared apixaban (at a dose of 5 mg twice daily) with warfarin (target international normalized ratio, 2.0 to 3.0) in 18,201 patients with atrial fibrillation

inclusion_criteria.text: Atrial fibrillation and at least one additional risk factor for stroke.
inclusion_criteria.quote: 18,201 patients with atrial fibrillation and at least one additional risk factor for stroke.

inclusion_criteria.text: Atrial fibrillation or flutter at enrollment or two or more episodes documented by ECG at least 2 weeks apart in prior 12 months.
inclusion_criteria.quote: Eligible patients had atrial fibrillation or flutter at enrollment or two or more episodes of atrial fi- brillation or flutter, as documented by electrocar- diography, at least 2 weeks apart in the 12 months before enrollment.

inclusion_criteria.text: At least one required stroke risk factor: age ≥75, prior stroke/TIA/systemic embolism, recent symptomatic heart failure or LVEF ≤40%, diabetes, or hypertension requiring pharmacologic treatment.
inclusion_criteria.quote: In addition, at least one of the following risk factors for stroke was required: an age of at least 75 years; previous stroke, transient ischemic attack, or systemic embolism; symptom- atic heart failure within the previous 3 months or left ventricular ejection fraction of no more than 40%; diabetes mellitus; or hypertension requiring pharmacologic treatment.
